en.title: Backend Engineering
en.description: Tracks covering the parts of backend work that break in production.

id.title: Backend Engineering
id.description: Kumpulan track yang membahas bagian backend yang paling sering jebol di produksi.

en.name: Indexing & Query Plans
en.description: How the planner actually chooses, and why your index is ignored.

id.name: Indexing & Query Plan
id.description: Cara planner benar-benar memilih, dan kenapa index kamu diabaikan.

en.stem_md: You have `CREATE INDEX idx ON bookings (status, created_at)`. Which query can use that index for the filter **and** the sort, with no separate sort step?
en.explanation_md: Leftmost prefix rule: a composite index is only usable left to right, with no gaps.

id.stem_md: Kamu punya index `CREATE INDEX idx ON bookings (status, created_at)`. Query mana yang bisa memakai index itu untuk filter **dan** sort sekaligus, tanpa langkah sort terpisah?
id.explanation_md: Leftmost prefix rule: index komposit hanya berguna dari kolom paling kiri ke kanan, tanpa bolong.

en.label_md: `WHERE created_at > '2026-01-01' ORDER BY status`
en.option_explanation_md: The leading column is skipped, so the index is only reachable through a full index scan.

id.label_md: `WHERE created_at > '2026-01-01' ORDER BY status`
id.option_explanation_md: Kolom paling kiri dilewati, jadi index hanya bisa dipakai lewat full index scan.

en.label_md: `WHERE status = 'pending' ORDER BY created_at DESC`
en.option_explanation_md: One value on the first column, then ordered by the second. The index is already in that order, and a backward scan is free.

id.label_md: `WHERE status = 'pending' ORDER BY created_at DESC`
id.option_explanation_md: Satu nilai di kolom pertama, lalu urut di kolom kedua. Index sudah terurut begitu, backward scan pun gratis.

en.label_md: `WHERE status IN ('pending','paid') ORDER BY created_at`
en.option_explanation_md: Two status values means two separately ordered ranges. The planner still has to merge or sort.

id.label_md: `WHERE status IN ('pending','paid') ORDER BY created_at`
id.option_explanation_md: Dua nilai status berarti dua rentang terurut terpisah. Planner masih harus merge atau sort.

en.label_md: `ORDER BY created_at, status` with no WHERE
en.option_explanation_md: Column order is reversed from the index, and there is no filter.

id.label_md: `ORDER BY created_at, status` tanpa WHERE
id.option_explanation_md: Urutan kolom kebalik dari index, dan tanpa filter.

en.stem_md: `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on a report page produces this. What does it tell you?
en.code_snippet:
-> Nested Loop  (actual time=0.004..214.9 rows=8412 loops=1)
      -> Seq Scan on bookings  (rows=8412 loops=1)
      -> Index Scan using users_pkey  (rows=1 loops=8412)
en.explanation_md: The first thing to read in EXPLAIN is not cost, it is loops and the gap between estimated and actual rows.

id.stem_md: `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` sebuah halaman laporan mengeluarkan baris ini. Apa artinya?
id.code_snippet:
-> Nested Loop  (actual time=0.004..214.9 rows=8412 loops=1)
      -> Seq Scan on bookings  (rows=8412 loops=1)
      -> Index Scan using users_pkey  (rows=1 loops=8412)
id.explanation_md: Yang dibaca pertama di EXPLAIN bukan cost, tapi loops dan selisih estimated vs actual rows.

en.label_md: The `users_pkey` index is unused and needs a `REINDEX`
en.option_explanation_md: The index is being used. The problem is how many times it is called.

id.label_md: Index `users_pkey` tidak terpakai dan perlu di-`REINDEX`
id.option_explanation_md: Index justru terpakai. Masalahnya berapa kali dia dipanggil.

en.label_md: A nested loop doing one lookup per outer row — an N+1 that moved into the planner
en.option_explanation_md: `loops=8412` means that index scan ran 8,412 times. Correct result, expensive total.

id.label_md: Nested loop yang menjalankan satu lookup per baris outer — N+1 yang pindah ke dalam planner
id.option_explanation_md: `loops=8412` artinya index scan itu dieksekusi 8.412 kali. Benar hasilnya, mahal totalnya.

en.label_md: Stale table statistics, needs an `ANALYZE`
en.option_explanation_md: A reasonable distractor, but estimated and actual rows match here.

id.label_md: Statistik tabel basi, perlu `ANALYZE`
id.option_explanation_md: Distraktor yang masuk akal, tapi estimasi dan actual rows di sini cocok.

en.label_md: The `bookings` table is missing an index on its foreign key
en.option_explanation_md: The seq scan on bookings is intentional, since every row is needed.

id.label_md: Tabel `bookings` kekurangan index pada foreign key
id.option_explanation_md: Seq scan pada bookings disengaja karena semua baris dibutuhkan.

en.stem_md: Two workers run this block at the same time on PostgreSQL at the default `READ COMMITTED`. Balance starts at 100, both deduct 50. What is the final balance?
en.explanation_md: Three fixes: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, an atomic `SET balance = balance - 50`, or a `version` column for optimistic locking.

id.stem_md: Dua worker menjalankan blok ini bersamaan di PostgreSQL dengan isolation default `READ COMMITTED`. Saldo awal 100, keduanya memotong 50. Berapa saldo akhirnya?
id.explanation_md: Perbaikannya ada tiga: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, `SET balance = balance - 50` yang atomik, atau kolom `version` untuk optimistic locking.

en.label_md: 0 — both deductions land
en.option_explanation_md: That is what you expect, not what happens.

id.label_md: 0 — kedua pemotongan masuk
id.option_explanation_md: Itu yang kamu harapkan, bukan yang terjadi.

en.label_md: 50 — the second transaction overwrites with a value computed from stale data
en.option_explanation_md: A lost update. Both read 100, both write 50. One deduction vanishes with no error.

id.label_md: 50 — transaksi kedua menimpa dengan nilai hasil hitungan data basi
id.option_explanation_md: Lost update. Keduanya membaca 100, keduanya menulis 50. Satu pemotongan hilang tanpa error.

en.label_md: The second transaction fails with a serialization error
en.option_explanation_md: That is `REPEATABLE READ` or `SERIALIZABLE` behaviour.

id.label_md: Transaksi kedua gagal dengan serialization error
id.option_explanation_md: Itu perilaku `REPEATABLE READ` atau `SERIALIZABLE`.

en.label_md: 100 — Postgres rolls both back
en.option_explanation_md: No conflict is detected, so nothing is rolled back.

id.label_md: 100 — Postgres me-rollback keduanya
id.option_explanation_md: Tidak ada konflik yang terdeteksi, jadi tidak ada yang di-rollback.

en.stem_md: The `/api/v1/leaderboard` response is cached in Redis for 60 seconds. At a peak of 4,000 req/s, the moment the key expires database CPU pins at 100% for two seconds. Which fix is right?
en.explanation_md: Three patterns worth memorising: a lock around the rebuild, refresh-ahead before expiry, and jittered TTLs so keys do not expire in lockstep.

id.stem_md: Endpoint `/api/v1/leaderboard` di-cache 60 detik di Redis. Saat puncak 4.000 req/s, tepat ketika key expire, CPU database melonjak 100% selama dua detik. Perbaikan mana yang benar?
id.explanation_md: Tiga pola yang perlu dihafal: lock saat rebuild, refresh-ahead sebelum expire, dan TTL yang di-jitter supaya key tidak expire serempak.

en.label_md: Drop the TTL to 10 seconds so the data stays fresher
en.option_explanation_md: That makes it worse: a stampede every 10 seconds instead of every 60.

id.label_md: Turunkan TTL jadi 10 detik supaya datanya lebih segar
id.option_explanation_md: Memperparah: stampede yang tadinya tiap 60 detik jadi tiap 10 detik.

en.label_md: Add a short lock — one request rebuilds the value while the rest serve the stale copy
en.option_explanation_md: This is a cache stampede, and the cure is letting exactly one rebuild through. Redis `SET NX EX` is enough.

id.label_md: Pasang lock singkat — satu request membangun ulang nilainya, sisanya menyajikan salinan basi
id.option_explanation_md: Ini cache stampede, dan obatnya memang satu rebuild saja yang lewat. Redis `SET NX EX` cukup.

en.label_md: Move the cache into process memory on each app server
en.option_explanation_md: Now you have N copies expiring at nearly the same time, and servers can disagree.

id.label_md: Pindahkan cache ke memory proses di setiap app server
id.option_explanation_md: Jadi N salinan yang expire hampir bersamaan, plus data antar server bisa beda.

en.label_md: Add a read replica to absorb the query spike
en.option_explanation_md: Treating the symptom with hardware. The spike still happens.

id.label_md: Tambah read replica untuk menampung lonjakan query
id.option_explanation_md: Mengobati gejala dengan hardware. Lonjakannya tetap terjadi.

en.stem_md: A client sends `POST /users` with `{"email": "not-an-email"}`. The JSON parses fine; your validator rejects the email. Which status fits best?
en.explanation_md: 400 means the server could not understand the request. 422 means it understood it and the content is still unacceptable.

id.stem_md: Client mengirim `POST /users` dengan `{"email": "not-an-email"}`. JSON-nya ter-parse normal; validator kamu menolak email itu. Status mana yang paling tepat?
id.explanation_md: 400 berarti server tidak bisa memahami request-nya. 422 berarti server paham, tapi isinya tetap tidak bisa diterima.

en.label_md: `400 Bad Request`
en.option_explanation_md: 400 is for a request the server cannot parse at all — broken JSON, a missing required header. This body parsed fine.

id.label_md: `400 Bad Request`
id.option_explanation_md: 400 untuk request yang tidak bisa di-parse sama sekali — JSON rusak, header wajib hilang. Body ini ter-parse normal.

en.label_md: `422 Unprocessable Entity`
en.option_explanation_md: The syntax was understood, the content was not acceptable. That is exactly 422, and it is what Laravel's validator returns.

id.label_md: `422 Unprocessable Entity`
id.option_explanation_md: Sintaksnya dipahami, isinya tidak bisa diterima. Itu persis 422, dan itu juga yang dikembalikan validator Laravel.

en.label_md: `200 OK` with `{"error": "..."}` in the body
en.option_explanation_md: The request did not succeed. Hiding the failure in a 200 forces every client, proxy and log to read the body before it knows what happened.

id.label_md: `200 OK` dengan `{"error": "..."}` di body
id.option_explanation_md: Request-nya tidak sukses. Menyembunyikan kegagalan di dalam 200 memaksa semua client, proxy, dan log membaca body dulu sebelum tahu apa yang terjadi.

en.label_md: `500 Internal Server Error`
en.option_explanation_md: Nothing broke on the server. A 500 tells the client to retry and wakes whoever is on call.

id.label_md: `500 Internal Server Error`
id.option_explanation_md: Tidak ada yang rusak di server. 500 menyuruh client retry dan membangunkan orang yang sedang on-call.

en.stem_md: `POST /exports` pushes a job onto a queue and returns immediately. The file does not exist yet. Which response is the honest one?
en.explanation_md: 202 is the only code that says "accepted, not finished". Everything else claims work that has not happened.

id.stem_md: `POST /exports` memasukkan job ke queue lalu langsung return. File-nya belum ada. Response mana yang jujur?
id.explanation_md: 202 satu-satunya kode yang bilang "diterima, belum selesai". Sisanya mengklaim kerjaan yang belum terjadi.

en.label_md: `201 Created` with a `Location` pointing at the export file
en.option_explanation_md: Nothing was created yet. A client that follows that Location gets a 404.

id.label_md: `201 Created` dengan `Location` menunjuk file export-nya
id.option_explanation_md: Belum ada apa pun yang dibuat. Client yang mengikuti Location itu akan dapat 404.

en.label_md: `202 Accepted` with a status URL the client can poll
en.option_explanation_md: 202 says the work is accepted but not finished, and the status URL gives the client somewhere to look.

id.label_md: `202 Accepted` dengan URL status yang bisa di-poll client
id.option_explanation_md: 202 bilang kerjaannya diterima tapi belum selesai, dan URL status memberi client tempat untuk mengecek.

en.label_md: `200 OK` with an empty body
en.option_explanation_md: 200 claims the request is done, and an empty body leaves the client with no handle on the job.

id.label_md: `200 OK` dengan body kosong
id.option_explanation_md: 200 mengklaim request-nya selesai, dan body kosong membuat client tidak punya pegangan apa pun ke job itu.

en.label_md: `204 No Content`
en.option_explanation_md: 204 means success with nothing to say. Here there is something to say: where to check on the job.

id.label_md: `204 No Content`
id.option_explanation_md: 204 berarti sukses tanpa ada yang perlu disampaikan. Di sini ada yang perlu disampaikan: di mana job-nya bisa dicek.

en.stem_md: A `products` table has a `tags` column holding `'postgres,indexing,wal'`. Which problem actually bites in production?
en.explanation_md: Naming the broken normal form is not the same as knowing what it costs. Here the cost is that no index can serve a tag filter.

id.stem_md: Tabel `products` punya kolom `tags` berisi `'postgres,indexing,wal'`. Masalah mana yang benar-benar terasa di produksi?
id.explanation_md: Menyebut normal form yang dilanggar beda dengan tahu biayanya. Di sini biayanya: tidak ada index yang bisa melayani filter per tag.

en.label_md: It breaks first normal form, so it is wrong by definition
en.option_explanation_md: True, and useless on its own. 1NF is the name of the problem, not the cost of it.

id.label_md: Itu melanggar first normal form, jadi salah secara definisi
id.option_explanation_md: Benar, tapi berdiri sendiri tidak berguna. 1NF adalah nama masalahnya, bukan biayanya.

en.label_md: No index can serve one tag, so every tag filter becomes `LIKE '%wal%'` over the whole table — and it also matches `wal-archive`
en.option_explanation_md: That is the real bill: a sequential scan on every filter, plus wrong rows from substring matches.

id.label_md: Tidak ada index yang bisa melayani satu tag, jadi setiap filter tag jadi `LIKE '%wal%'` ke seluruh tabel — dan itu juga kena `wal-archive`
id.option_explanation_md: Itu tagihan sebenarnya: sequential scan di setiap filter, plus baris salah karena substring.

en.label_md: The column will eventually run out of space
en.option_explanation_md: A Postgres `text` column grows to about a gigabyte. Size is not what hurts here.

id.label_md: Kolomnya akan kehabisan ruang
id.option_explanation_md: Kolom `text` di Postgres bisa sampai sekitar satu gigabyte. Yang sakit di sini bukan ukuran.

en.label_md: The tag names repeat on every row, which wastes disk
en.option_explanation_md: Real, but minor. Duplication costs disk once; the missing index costs latency on every single query.

id.label_md: Nama tag berulang di tiap baris, jadi buang-buang disk
id.option_explanation_md: Nyata, tapi kecil. Duplikasi membayar disk sekali; index yang tidak ada membayar latensi di setiap query.

en.stem_md: `order_lines` stores `unit_price` even though `products.price` already exists. A reviewer calls it denormalisation and asks you to drop the column and join instead. What do you answer?
en.explanation_md: Two columns that look like duplicates can mean different things. `products.price` is today's price; `order_lines.unit_price` is what this customer was charged.

id.stem_md: `order_lines` menyimpan `unit_price` padahal `products.price` sudah ada. Reviewer menyebutnya denormalisasi dan minta kolomnya dihapus lalu di-join saja. Apa jawabanmu?
id.explanation_md: Dua kolom yang kelihatan duplikat bisa punya makna berbeda. `products.price` adalah harga hari ini; `order_lines.unit_price` adalah harga yang ditagihkan ke pelanggan itu.

en.label_md: Keep it — `products.price` is today's price, the order needs the price at the time it was placed
en.option_explanation_md: The two columns answer different questions. Joining would silently rewrite old invoices every time someone edits a price.

id.label_md: Pertahankan — `products.price` itu harga hari ini, order butuh harga saat order dibuat
id.option_explanation_md: Dua kolom itu menjawab pertanyaan berbeda. Join akan diam-diam mengubah invoice lama setiap kali ada yang mengedit harga.

en.label_md: Drop it — the join is cheap and normalisation wins
en.option_explanation_md: The join is cheap. It is also wrong: it answers "what does this cost now", not "what did they pay".

id.label_md: Hapus — join-nya murah dan normalisasi lebih penting
id.option_explanation_md: Join-nya murah. Tapi juga salah: itu menjawab "sekarang harganya berapa", bukan "dia bayar berapa".

en.label_md: Drop it and add `price_changed_at` on `products`
en.option_explanation_md: One timestamp does not reconstruct a price history, and it still cannot tell you what this order was charged.

id.label_md: Hapus, lalu tambah `price_changed_at` di `products`
id.option_explanation_md: Satu timestamp tidak bisa merekonstruksi riwayat harga, dan tetap tidak bisa bilang order ini ditagih berapa.

en.label_md: Keep both and add a trigger that keeps `unit_price` equal to `products.price`
en.option_explanation_md: That deletes the only reason the column exists. Now the invoice changes under the customer.

id.label_md: Pertahankan keduanya dan tambah trigger yang menjaga `unit_price` sama dengan `products.price`
id.option_explanation_md: Itu menghapus satu-satunya alasan kolom itu ada. Sekarang invoice-nya berubah di belakang pelanggan.

en.stem_md: A high-write table uses a random `uuid` (v4) as its primary key instead of a monotonically increasing `bigint`. Inside the B-Tree, which effect dominates the extra write cost?
en.explanation_md: A B-Tree stores keys in sorted order, so where a key lands is decided by its value. Random values land everywhere; increasing values land in one place.

id.stem_md: Tabel dengan write tinggi memakai `uuid` (v4) acak sebagai primary key, bukan `bigint` yang naik terus. Di dalam B-Tree, efek mana yang paling menentukan tambahan biaya write-nya?
id.explanation_md: B-Tree menyimpan key dalam urutan terurut, jadi posisi sebuah key ditentukan nilainya. Nilai acak jatuh di mana-mana; nilai yang naik jatuh di satu tempat.

en.label_md: Every insert lands on a random leaf page, so writes touch pages that are no longer in cache and split them in the middle
en.option_explanation_md: Random keys spread writes across the whole index. An increasing key keeps appending to the rightmost leaf, which stays hot in cache and splits cleanly.

id.label_md: Tiap insert jatuh di leaf page acak, jadi write menyentuh page yang sudah tidak ada di cache dan membelahnya di tengah
id.option_explanation_md: Key acak menyebarkan write ke seluruh index. Key yang naik terus hanya menambah di leaf paling kanan, yang tetap panas di cache dan terbelah bersih.

en.label_md: The tree gets deeper, because a 16-byte key fits fewer entries per page than an 8-byte one
en.option_explanation_md: That part is true and does cost something, but a level or two of depth is small next to dirtying and splitting random pages on every insert.

id.label_md: Tree-nya jadi lebih dalam, karena key 16 byte memuat lebih sedikit entri per page daripada 8 byte
id.option_explanation_md: Bagian itu benar dan ada biayanya, tapi satu-dua level kedalaman kecil dibanding mengotori dan membelah page acak di setiap insert.

en.label_md: Lookups degrade to a full scan, because UUIDs have no natural order
en.option_explanation_md: The index still stores them in sorted byte order. A lookup is still a tree descent of a few pages.

id.label_md: Lookup turun jadi full scan, karena UUID tidak punya urutan alami
id.option_explanation_md: Index tetap menyimpannya terurut secara byte. Lookup tetap turun beberapa page lewat tree.

en.label_md: Nothing changes — a B-Tree rebalances itself either way
en.option_explanation_md: It does rebalance itself. The question is what that rebalancing costs, and with random keys it costs splits on cold pages.

id.label_md: Tidak ada yang berubah — B-Tree menyeimbangkan dirinya sendiri
id.option_explanation_md: Benar dia menyeimbangkan diri. Pertanyaannya berapa biayanya, dan dengan key acak biayanya adalah split di page yang dingin.

en.stem_md: `orders` has 10M rows and an index on `is_paid`, where 92% of rows are `true`. `WHERE is_paid = true` still plans a Seq Scan. Why is the planner right?
en.explanation_md: An index scan pays a heap fetch per matching row, and those fetches are scattered. Past a few percent of the table, one ordered pass over the heap wins.

id.stem_md: `orders` punya 10 juta baris dan index di `is_paid`, di mana 92% barisnya `true`. `WHERE is_paid = true` tetap direncanakan sebagai Seq Scan. Kenapa planner-nya benar?
id.explanation_md: Index scan membayar satu heap fetch per baris yang cocok, dan fetch-nya tersebar. Lewat beberapa persen dari tabel, satu lintasan terurut ke heap lebih murah.

en.label_md: Reading 9.2M rows through the index means 9.2M scattered heap fetches, which costs more than reading the table once in physical order
en.option_explanation_md: Selectivity, not the existence of an index, decides this. The index wins when it eliminates most of the table, and here it eliminates 8%.

id.label_md: Membaca 9,2 juta baris lewat index berarti 9,2 juta heap fetch yang tersebar, lebih mahal daripada membaca tabel sekali dalam urutan fisik
id.option_explanation_md: Yang menentukan selektivitas, bukan ada-tidaknya index. Index menang kalau membuang sebagian besar tabel, dan di sini dia hanya membuang 8%.

en.label_md: Postgres never uses an index on a boolean column
en.option_explanation_md: It will. `WHERE is_paid = false` hits the other 8%, and there the same index is a good choice.

id.label_md: Postgres tidak pernah memakai index di kolom boolean
id.option_explanation_md: Dia memakainya. `WHERE is_paid = false` kena 8% sisanya, dan di situ index yang sama adalah pilihan bagus.

en.label_md: The statistics are stale and `ANALYZE` would bring the index back
en.option_explanation_md: Stale statistics cause plenty of bad plans, but here the statistics are right and so is the plan.

id.label_md: Statistiknya basi dan `ANALYZE` akan membuat index terpakai lagi
id.option_explanation_md: Statistik basi memang sering bikin plan buruk, tapi di sini statistiknya benar dan plan-nya juga benar.

en.label_md: The index is bloated and needs a `REINDEX`
en.option_explanation_md: Bloat makes an index scan worse, not a seq scan better. Even a freshly built index loses this one.

id.label_md: Index-nya bloat dan perlu `REINDEX`
id.option_explanation_md: Bloat membuat index scan makin buruk, bukan membuat seq scan makin bagus. Index yang baru dibangun pun kalah di kasus ini.

en.title: Seven Days
en.description: Answer at least one question on seven consecutive days.

id.title: Tujuh Hari
id.description: Jawab minimal satu soal selama tujuh hari berturut-turut.

en.title: Clean Queue
en.description: Clear the whole review queue in one day.

id.title: Antrean Bersih
id.description: Habiskan seluruh antrean review dalam satu hari.
